action_rule: Exactly one visual action per sentence; planned action onset == sentence planned_start (build tolerance ±0.3 s).

rows.sentence: Nearby galaxies are rich in oxygen — but was that already true when the universe was young?
rows.action: presenter on camera; title line rises

rows.sentence: Five carefully chosen galaxies let us check.
rows.action: five dots appear beside presenter

rows.sentence: A galaxy's oxygen abundance is how much oxygen its gas holds.
rows.action: CG_A reveals: galaxy outline with gas shading

rows.sentence: Stars forge that oxygen, so it grows as galaxies build stars.
rows.action: star symbols pulse; oxygen level bar rises

rows.sentence: So oxygen works like a clock for a galaxy's history.
rows.action: clock-hand motif sweeps over the rising bar

rows.sentence: This paper asks: at redshift nine to ten, very early, had galaxies already reached nearby oxygen levels?
rows.action: question card types on

rows.sentence: There are two traps.
rows.action: split panel opens (two empty trap slots)

rows.sentence: Gravitational lensing magnifies a distant galaxy, and it can distort the mass we infer.
rows.action: lensed light path bends; mass readout wobbles

rows.sentence: And the nearby benchmark is extrapolated below the masses where it was measured.
rows.action: benchmark line turns dashed past its measured range

rows.sentence: So the paper picks five strictly unlensed galaxies, at redshift nine point three to nine point nine.
rows.action: unlensed side highlights; five markers land

rows.sentence: Their oxygen comes from direct electron-temperature measurements, all on one consistent scale.
rows.action: method chip stamps on

rows.sentence: Here is the paper's real data figure.
rows.action: FIG1 slides in full-frame

rows.sentence: Across runs each galaxy's stellar mass, and up runs its gas oxygen abundance.
rows.action: axis sweep highlight (x then y)

rows.sentence: These curves show the nearby benchmark relations.
rows.action: both benchmark curves glow

rows.sentence: Now the five unlensed galaxies appear — the red circles.
rows.action: zoom to red-point cluster; points pulse once

rows.sentence: Every one sits below the benchmark, near one fifth of the nearby level.
rows.action: gap bracket draws from points up to the curve

rows.sentence: In logarithmic units, the average shortfall is zero point six nine dex, with a small spread.
rows.action: value label −0.69 ± 0.03 dex draws on the bracket

rows.sentence: What if the benchmark itself misleads — swap it for one measured at exactly these masses.
rows.action: emphasis shifts from extrapolated curve to measured curve

rows.sentence: The shortfall barely moves: about zero point six five dex.
rows.action: second label ≈−0.65 dex draws beside measured curve

rows.sentence: One more check is fully independent.
rows.action: CG_D reveals: many faint spectra rows

rows.sentence: Roughly fifteen hundred fainter galaxies are stacked into one combined measurement.
rows.action: spectra rows collapse into a single point

rows.sentence: Back on the figure, the blue square is that stack — about zero point five to zero point six dex low.
rows.action: cut to FIG1; blue square rings and labels

rows.sentence: The famous galaxy G N z eleven, at redshift ten point six, agrees in direction with larger uncertainty.
rows.action: GN-z11 info chip slides in beside the figure

rows.sentence: What could still bend this result?
rows.action: CG_E reveals: two empty comparison bars

rows.sentence: The absolute temperature-based abundance scale is debated at the level of zero point one to zero point two dex.
rows.action: uncertainty band bar fills to 0.1–0.2 dex

rows.sentence: That is smaller than the shortfall, but it limits how precisely we know its size.
rows.action: deficit bar (0.69 dex) rises beside the band for comparison

rows.sentence: And only five galaxies carry the redshift nine-to-ten result.
rows.action: five sample markers blink on the budget panel

rows.sentence: Machine-generated by an autonomous research pipeline; descriptive, not validated; automated review is not journal or human peer review.
rows.action: warning-styled boundary card slides up

rows.sentence: This is not a formal statistical detection.
rows.action: boundary line underlines once

rows.sentence: So: five clean galaxies, one consistent scale, and an oxygen shortfall that survives the benchmark swap.
rows.action: return to FIG1 gap view; bracket re-glows

rows.sentence: The full paper is at nebulamind dot net — descriptive, not validated.
rows.action: presenter returns; URL card shows

cold_reader.instructions: Reader must not have seen the paper or prior videos. Give them the script audio (or read-through) plus the storyboard stills. Closed-book answers.
questions: Q1: What physical quantity is this paper measuring in galaxies?
Q2: What is the paper's main question?
Q3: Why does the paper use only unlensed galaxies?
Q4: What does the main figure show, and where do the five galaxies sit?
Q5: What happens to the result when the nearby benchmark is swapped for one measured at these masses?
Q6: What independent cross-check supports the result?
Q7: What is the dominant remaining uncertainty?
Q8: What does the paper explicitly NOT claim?
answer_key: A1: The oxygen abundance of galaxy gas (gas-phase metallicity).
A2: Whether galaxies at redshift nine to ten had already reached nearby oxygen levels.
A3: Because gravitational lensing can distort the inferred galaxy masses.
A4: Stellar mass across, gas oxygen abundance up; the five red-circle galaxies all sit below the nearby benchmark, near one fifth of it (about 0.69 dex low).
A5: It barely changes — about minus 0.65 dex instead of minus 0.69.
A6: A stack of roughly fifteen hundred fainter galaxies, landing about 0.5 to 0.6 dex low (GN-z11 direction agreement also acceptable).
A7: The absolute temperature-based abundance scale (0.1–0.2 dex), plus the small five-galaxy sample.
A8: A formal statistical detection (it is descriptive, machine-generated, not validated).
cold_reader.pass_rule: ≥ 7 of 8 answers substantively correct, and Q8 must be among the correct ones. Fail ⇒ rewrite narration and repeat V5-G2; no facial animation until pass.
